articles.title: Comparison of novel anterior fixation method, W-plate, versus superior parasymphyseal plating in anterior posterior compression type III pelvic ring injuries: a biomechanical study.
articles.authors: Krieg BA, Baldini T, Orear C, Onodera KM, Tucker NJ, Schlauch A, et al.
articles.population: Composite pelvic models with anterior posterior compression type III pelvic ring injuries
articles.outcomes: Stiffness, displacement, and load to failure of W-plate versus superior parasymphyseal plating under simulated single leg stance and external rotation loading
articles.take_home: W-plating and superior parasymphyseal plating performed similarly in a laboratory test of pelvic stability, with W-plating showing slightly less forward movement of the pubic bone but no significant differences in overall strength or stiffness.

articles.title: Mechanical Failure and Revision Risk Following Transition from PFNA to TFNA: A Single-Center Cohort Study of 1,970 Patients.
articles.authors: Ben Zoor I, Fogel I, Balaziano S, Goldstein B, Mansor Y, Friedlander A, et al.
articles.population: Patients aged over 65 years with hip fractures treated with cephalomedullary nails at a single trauma centre
articles.outcomes: Implant mechanical failure, cut-out rate, time to failure, and mortality within revision-risk window
articles.take_home: The newer TFNA nail had a five-fold higher rate of mechanical failure and four-fold higher rate of cut-outs compared to the older PFNA nail, with failures occurring earlier. Surgeons should be particularly cautious when using TFNA in heavier patients.

articles.title: Headless Compression Screws May Reduce Symptomatic Hardware After Medial Malleolus Fixation: A Comparative Cohort Study.
articles.authors: Rechter GR, Langford JR, Shaath MK, Baker TB, Page BE, Yawman J, et al.
articles.population: Skeletally mature patients with medial malleolus fractures treated with surgery
articles.outcomes: Symptomatic hardware, hardware removal rates, fracture healing, and infection rates
articles.take_home: Headless compression screws resulted in fewer patients experiencing bothersome hardware symptoms (21% versus 35%) compared to traditional headed screws, without affecting bone healing or infection rates. Hardware removal rates were similar between both types of screw.

articles.title: Diagnostic accuracy of shock index, revised trauma score, and injury severity score for mortality prediction in trauma: A hierarchical meta-analysis.
articles.authors: Raza AA, Ahmad M, Choudhary N, Rehman A, Zahid M, Rehman A, et al.
articles.population: Adult trauma patients
articles.outcomes: In-hospital mortality prediction; diagnostic accuracy (sensitivity, specificity, AUC) of Shock Index, Revised Trauma Score, and Injury Severity Score
articles.take_home: Revised Trauma Score and Injury Severity Score performed similarly well at predicting death in trauma patients, with no significant difference between them. These scoring tools work best when used at different stages of trauma care rather than as competing alternatives.

articles.title: Epidemiological patterns and surgical outcomes of pediatric supracondylar humerus fractures: a focus on domestic safety and seasonal variations.
articles.authors: Altin R, Cakirturk S, Erten RA, Ozdemir S, Yesil M, Yilmaz BK
articles.population: Children aged 14 years and under with supracondylar humerus fractures
articles.outcomes: Functional outcomes using Flynn's criteria; radiological reduction assessed via Baumann angle and anterior humeral line; complication rates
articles.take_home: Most of these fractures happen at home during summer when children fall, but surgery with careful realignment produces excellent results in nearly 98% of cases with minimal lasting complications. Simple changes to make homes safer and better parental supervision could help prevent many of these injuries.

articles.title: Osteoporosis medication initiation after proximal humerus fractures is low, but associated with decreased secondary fragility fracture risk.
articles.authors: Ni A, Atkison CL, Williamson TK, Holdipp DI, Papanikolaou KN, Martin CW
articles.population: Patients aged 60 years or older with proximal humerus fractures
articles.sample_size: 180,304 patients with proximal humerus fractures; 6,627 (3.7%) prescribed osteoporosis medication
articles.outcomes: Prescription rates of osteoporosis medication after fracture; rates of secondary fragility fractures; 1-year mortality rates
articles.take_home: Very few older patients with broken shoulders receive osteoporosis medication after their fracture, but those who do have a lower risk of future fractures and lower death rates in the first year. Female patients were more likely to receive the medication than male patients, and Black patients were less likely to receive it.

articles.title: Estrogen hormonal therapy is not associated with increased risk of venous thrombosis in total hip arthroplasty or hemiarthroplasty for femoral neck fractures.
articles.authors: Ni A, Abdelrahim L, McDonald CD, Cal E, Lancaster CE, Martin CW
articles.population: Patients with femoral neck fractures treated with total hip arthroplasty or hemiarthroplasty
articles.outcomes: Deep vein thrombosis or pulmonary embolism within 3 months after fracture
articles.take_home: Women taking estrogen hormone therapy did not have a significantly higher risk of blood clots after hip surgery for femoral neck fractures compared to those not taking estrogen.

articles.title: Measuring Knee Alignment Following Distal Femur Fracture Surgery: A Novel Deep Learning Approach.
articles.authors: Pereira DE, Chakladar S, Harrison NJ, Rust BD, Obey MR, McAndrew CM, et al.
articles.population: Adults aged 50 years and older who had surgery for distal femur fractures
articles.sample_size: 287 postoperative radiographs from patients with mean age 72.3 years
articles.outcomes: Accuracy of automated machine learning measurements of knee alignment angles (JLCA, aFTA, aLDFA, aMPTA) compared to surgeon measurements
articles.take_home: A computer system using artificial intelligence can accurately measure knee alignment from standard X-rays after distal femur fracture surgery, with measurements within 1 to 2 degrees of those done by surgeons. This automated approach could help doctors monitor knee alignment over time in routine follow-up care.

articles.title: Injury patterns in a war zone: A comparative analysis of civilians and military personnel.
articles.authors: Sasson I, Chaushu H, Ungar OJ
articles.population: Civilians and defence forces treated at a single tertiary trauma centre during active conflict
articles.outcomes: Injury mechanisms, anatomical injury patterns, injury severity (ISS), emergency interventions, and early clinical outcomes including ICU admission and operating room transfer rates
articles.take_home: Civilians and defence forces suffered similarly severe injuries overall, but had different injury patterns. Civilians were much more likely to have acoustic trauma (hearing damage from blast), whilst defence forces more often had shrapnel injuries and needed emergency surgery more frequently.

articles.title: Force measurement in circular external fixation frames reflects construct stability: A laboratory proof-of-concept study.
articles.authors: Naeem H, Maroy R, Stewart T, Harwood P, Howard A
articles.population: Simulated fracture healing models using Perspex bone analogue
articles.sample_size: Three four-ring Ilizarov frame constructs with multiple measurements across different sensor positions
articles.outcomes: Force measurements within the frame decreased with increasing construct stiffness; significant relationship between stability and measured force observed (p < 0.0001); strong discrimination between unstable and intact constructs (AUC >/= 0.91) but reduced discrimination between higher stability models and intact bone (AUC 0.699-0.838)
articles.take_home: Measuring the force within an external fixation frame can reflect how stable the fracture site is becoming. The researchers suggest that tracking these measurements over time in patients might help doctors decide when it is safe to remove the frame, though this needs testing in real patients first.

articles.title: Screening for posttraumatic stress symptoms after accidental injury: Implementation of the young child PTSD screen in the acute trauma setting.
articles.authors: Ray M, Bailey A, Lendrum E, Vore E, Poundstone A, Beiting S, et al.
articles.population: Children aged 2-6 years admitted to a Level I paediatric trauma centre following unintentional injury
articles.outcomes: Screening positivity for post-traumatic stress symptoms using the Young Child PTSD Screen at hospital discharge and one month follow-up; predictors of positive screening and symptom persistence
articles.take_home: More than half of young children screened positive for post-traumatic stress symptoms when tested at discharge from hospital after accidental injury, and over 40 per cent still showed symptoms one month later. Children with more severe injuries were more likely to screen positive, and those with higher symptoms at discharge were more likely to have ongoing symptoms.

articles.title: Survival and Reoperation After Intralesional Procedures Versus Resection and Reconstruction for Renal Cell Carcinoma Bone Metastases.
articles.authors: Kashyap J, Carlson LA, Garvin LE 2nd, Schoedel KE, Lohse I, Lee SJ, et al.
articles.population: Patients with renal cell carcinoma bone metastases in long bones
articles.outcomes: Survival, reoperation rates, and complications following intralesional procedures versus resection and reconstruction
articles.take_home: Intralesional procedures were associated with higher mortality overall, but this difference was not seen in patients with a single metastasis. Both surgical approaches had similar reoperation rates, suggesting both can be reasonable options depending on individual patient circumstances.

articles.title: Pathological fracture as initial manifestation of malignancy and survival based on diagnoses: a register-based cohort study from the Swedish Fracture Register and the Swedish Cancer Register.
articles.authors: Sundkvist J, Giaever J, Wennergren D, Crnalic S, Wanman J
articles.population: Patients with pathological fracture as initial manifestation of malignancy
articles.outcomes: Survival by cancer type; mortality risk factors including age and tumour site
articles.take_home: When patients present with a broken bone that turns out to be caused by cancer, blood cancers were most common, but lung cancer patients had the worst survival. Survival was generally short and depended on the type of cancer and the patient's age.

articles.title: Comparison of suicidal and accidental fall injury patterns: A 10-year retrospective study in Hong Kong.
articles.authors: Hui LH, Hau ESS, Leung LY, Cheung RKH, Cheung NK, Man SY, et al.
articles.population: Patients aged 18 years and over admitted to a tertiary hospital in Hong Kong after falling from a height of 2 metres or more
articles.outcomes: Injury severity score, abbreviated injury scale scores, types of fractures sustained, and clinical outcomes including mortality
articles.take_home: People who fall accidentally from height are more likely to suffer serious head and neck injuries and these are often fatal, whilst people who fall intentionally tend to have more serious injuries to the abdomen and lower body. Accidental falls tend to involve lower heights but result in more severe head trauma.

articles.title: Clinical application and effectiveness analysis of the InterTan nail in the treatment of femoral neck fractures.
articles.authors: Liu H, He J, Li M, Augustine Q, Wang P, Liu X, et al.
articles.population: Adults aged 65 years or under with high-energy displaced femoral neck fractures
articles.outcomes: Fracture union, femoral neck shortening, Harris Hip Score, complications, reoperation rate
articles.take_home: All 25 patients achieved fracture union with the InterTan nail, with minimal femoral neck shortening and only one patient (4%) needing further surgery within 2 years for bone death of the femoral head. At 2 years, patients reported good hip function with a mean Harris Hip Score of 90.8.

articles.title: Outcomes Following Early Weight Bearing in Syndesmotic Injuries: A Randomized Controlled Trial.
articles.authors: Khaleel M, Durante E, Hawkins S, Stannard JP, Della Rocca GJ, Crist B, et al.
articles.population: Adult patients with rotational ankle fractures and syndesmotic injury treated with operative fixation and single suture button stabilization
articles.sample_size: 39 patients completed the study (16 early weight bearing, 23 delayed weight bearing)
articles.outcomes: Primary: maintenance of syndesmotic reduction at 1 year on CT scan. Secondary: pain scores, surgical satisfaction, functional scores, ankle range of motion, complications, and arthritis development
articles.take_home: Patients who began weight bearing at 2 weeks had slightly more pain initially but achieved better ankle bending at 1 year compared to those who waited 6 weeks, with no differences in joint positioning, satisfaction, or long-term complications. Early weight bearing appears safe and effective after ankle fracture surgery with syndesmotic stabilization.

articles.title: Mini Fragment T-Plate Fixation for Medial Malleolar Fractures Achieves Comparable Outcomes to Small Fragment Screw Fixation Without Increased Complication Risk.
articles.authors: Lau E, Saggar R, Olawin A, Li K, Moloney G
articles.population: Adults aged 18 years and over with medial malleolar ankle fractures treated at a single level I trauma centre
articles.sample_size: 141 patients (68 treated with mini fragment T-plate, 73 with small fragment screw fixation)
articles.outcomes: Infection rates, nonunion rates, reoperation rates, symptomatic hardware complications, and time to weight bearing
articles.take_home: Mini fragment T-plate fixation and traditional screw fixation produced similar results for medial malleolar fractures, with no significant differences in infection, reoperation, or failure rates. Mini fragment T-plate fixation is a viable alternative option when fracture shape makes dual-screw placement unsafe.

articles.title: The Association Between Serum Inflammatory Markers and Pathogen Profile in Confirmed Fracture-related Infection.
articles.authors: Ganta A, Merrell LA, Vu NH, Solasz SJ, Konda SR, Egol KA
articles.population: Patients with confirmed fracture-related infection treated between January 2011 and July 2024
articles.sample_size: 359 patients (331 with ESR values, 343 with CRP values)
articles.outcomes: Erythrocyte Sedimentation Rate (ESR) and C-reactive protein (CRP) levels compared across four pathogen groups: gram-positive monomicrobial, gram-negative monomicrobial, polymicrobial, and culture-negative infections
articles.take_home: CRP levels were roughly 2.5 times higher in gram-positive infections compared with gram-negative infections, but this difference is not reliable enough to identify the type of bacteria causing a fracture-related infection in individual patients. ESR did not vary meaningfully between infection types.

articles.title: Dynamic Interfragmentary Compression Through a Tibial Intramedullary Nail Compared to Backslapping Alone: A Biomechanical Analysis.
articles.authors: Haws BE, Thompson JD, Yawman JP, Davis JM, Suh N, Blair JA
articles.population: Synthetic tibial fracture models
articles.outcomes: Interfragmentary compression force measured at initial compression, before and after simulated three months of weightbearing loading
articles.take_home: Intramedullary nails with a dynamic internal compression device generated and maintained significantly greater compression forces across fracture fragments compared to manual backslapping alone. Both techniques lost some compressive force during simulated weightbearing, though the compression device maintained better force overall.

articles.title: Orthopaedic Care in Norway: Organization, Research, and Quality Improvement.
articles.authors: Solberg LB, Gjertsen JE, Inderhaug E, Frihagen F
articles.population: Population of Norway (5.6 million inhabitants)
articles.outcomes: Orthopaedic care quality, access to specialist services, clinical outcomes through quality registries, fracture prevention programmes
articles.take_home: Norway's publicly funded orthopaedic system uses national quality registries and clinician-led collaboration to monitor outcomes and continuously improve patient care. The system shows how universal healthcare, standardised pathways, and research integration can deliver equitable access to high-quality orthopaedic services.

articles.title: The rate of total hip arthroplasty after closed reduction of late-detected hip dislocation : 147 hips followed to patient age 70 years.
articles.authors: Terjesen T, Wensaas A
articles.study_type: Retrospective cohort study with registry follow-up
articles.population: Children aged under 3 years diagnosed with late-detected hip dislocation treated with closed reduction
articles.outcomes: Rate of total hip replacement by age 70 years; risk factors for replacement; survival rates with replacement as endpoint
articles.take_home: Children with late-detected hip dislocation who had closed reduction without additional surgery showed good long-term outcomes if their hip socket was normal-shaped when fully grown, with only 24% needing hip replacement by age 70. Those with ongoing socket abnormality had much worse outcomes, with 59% requiring replacement by age 70.

articles.title: Radiographic assessment of metacarpal shortening after nonoperative and operative treatment of spiral and oblique metacarpal shaft fractures.
articles.authors: Stalberg Ostwald C, Peyronson F, Hailer NP, Muder D
articles.study_type: Midterm follow-up of a randomised controlled trial
articles.population: Patients with a single spiral or oblique metacarpal shaft fracture
articles.outcomes: Metacarpal shortening measured by radiograph, extension deficit, cosmesis, and overall satisfaction
articles.take_home: Non-operative treatment of certain hand fractures resulted in an average 3.9 mm bone shortening compared to 0.9 mm with surgery, but this shortening did not affect hand function, appearance, or patient satisfaction at 4.5 years follow-up.

articles.title: Proximal humerus fractures: A review of current management evidence and guidance on contemporary surgical strategies.
articles.authors: Hoskins W, Haase D
articles.study_type: Narrative review with systematic search of randomised controlled trials
articles.population: Patients with proximal humerus fractures, including elderly osteoporotic women and younger patients with high-energy trauma
articles.outcomes: Treatment outcomes including fracture healing, functional recovery, complication rates and implant performance across non-operative management, internal fixation methods and arthroplasty options
articles.take_home: Treatment of proximal humerus fractures should be individualised based on age, health, function and fracture type. Locked plate surgery, traditionally most common, has high complication rates and is not better than non-operative treatment. Reverse shoulder replacement is increasingly used in elderly patients with promising results, although evidence comparing all treatment options remains limited.

articles.title: Patient centered outcomes after surgical stabilization of rib fractures: A prospective cohort study.
articles.authors: Laredo J, Walker M, Wilson F, Hertslet G, Heidel E, Lange K, et al.
articles.population: Trauma intensive care unit patients with rib fractures meeting criteria for surgical stabilisation (flail chest, 3 or more contiguous rib fractures, or ventilator failure)
articles.sample_size: 121 patients, of whom 39 (32%) underwent surgical stabilisation
articles.outcomes: Physical functioning and pain measured using SF-36 and SF-MPQ-2 questionnaires at discharge, 2 weeks, 3 months, and 6 months
articles.take_home: Surgical stabilisation of rib fractures was associated with better physical functioning at discharge and at 6 months compared to non-operative management, but did not result in long-term pain reduction. The surgery appears to help patients recover their ability to function more quickly rather than providing lasting pain relief.

articles.title: Thoracic irrigation for traumatic hemothorax: a cost-effective analysis.
articles.authors: Olivera Perez H, Huang Perez A, Gochi AM, Alcasid N, Thornblade L, Balan N, et al.
articles.population: Haemodynamically stable patients with traumatic hemothorax requiring chest tube drainage
articles.outcomes: Cost in US dollars, Quality-Adjusted Life Years (QALYs), net monetary benefit, need for secondary interventions such as VATS
articles.take_home: Thoracic irrigation after chest tube placement for traumatic hemothorax costs less money (about £14,000 versus £27,000) whilst providing slightly better quality of life compared to drainage alone. This strategy should be routinely considered as it reduces costs and may improve patient outcomes.

articles.title: Efficacy of topical vancomycin in preventing surgical site infection following fracture surgery : a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.authors: Badhe N, Hutton A, See A, Ollivere BJ, Marson BA
articles.study_type: Systematic review and meta-analysis of randomised controlled trials
articles.population: Patients undergoing surgical management of upper or lower limb fractures
articles.outcomes: Fracture-related infection, deep surgical site infection, superficial surgical site infection, nonunion, wound healing problems, renal impairment, and antimicrobial resistance
articles.take_home: Topical vancomycin powder applied during fracture surgery reduced the risk of infection compared with no treatment, particularly for infections caused by common bacteria. The treatment appeared safe with no significant kidney problems or other serious complications, though more large-scale studies are needed to confirm these findings.

articles.title: Clinical equipoise as inclusion criterion to control for confounding in observational studies.
articles.authors: van der Hoeven NM, Peuker F, Michelitsch C, Smeeing DPJ, Houwert RM, Beeres FJP, et al.
articles.population: Patients with proximal humerus fractures treated operatively or non-operatively
articles.outcomes: Baseline comparability between treatment groups (age, sex, ASA score, AO classification) across levels of expert disagreement about treatment choice
articles.take_home: When expert trauma surgeons disagreed most about what treatment a patient should have received, patients in the operative and non-operative groups were more similar at the start, suggesting this approach could reduce bias in studies where randomised trials are not possible. However, using stricter disagreement criteria meant fewer patients could be included in the analysis.

articles.title: Trauma governance and system maturity: A cross-national analysis of authority, funding, enforcement, and surveillance in 37 countries.
articles.authors: Kewalramani D, Benton J, Choron RL, Teichman A, Englert Z, Gelster C, et al.
articles.population: 37 countries across all World Bank regions and income levels (lower-middle, upper-middle, high income)
articles.sample_size: 37 countries; 15 had formal trauma governance entities
articles.outcomes: Trauma system maturity scores, injury mortality rate per 1000 persons, association between governance components and system maturity
articles.take_home: Countries with formal trauma governance structures had better organised trauma systems and lower death rates from injury compared to those without governance. The biggest improvement came from having any formal governance in place, rather than having more comprehensive governance.

articles.title: Predictors of prolonged emergency department length of stay in severely injured pediatric patients.
articles.authors: Cevik AA, Alao DO, Farooq M, Abu-Zidan F
articles.study_type: Retrospective analysis of prospectively collected registry data
articles.population: Severely injured children under 18 years old (Injury Severity Score over 12)
articles.outcomes: Factors associated with emergency department length of stay over 4 hours
articles.take_home: Children treated in teaching hospitals, those without trauma team activation, and those with certain injury types like road traffic collisions stayed longer in the emergency department. Surprisingly, children with more severe injuries actually had shorter stays, suggesting faster transfer to operating theatres.

articles.title: Pediatric perineal trauma: a prospective observational study of mechanisms, surgical management, and outcomes.
articles.authors: Ahmed E, Talat N, Afzal HMW, Adnan HM, Mahmood U
articles.population: Children with perineal trauma requiring surgery
articles.outcomes: Anal sphincter function, vaginal stenosis, cosmetic and functional outcomes. 82.1% had good anal sphincter function, no vaginal stenosis identified, three adverse outcomes occurred
articles.take_home: Most children with perineal injuries can be repaired primarily with good outcomes when assessed and managed by specialist teams. Delayed reconstruction may be needed for complex or infected injuries.

articles.title: From bowing to fracture : radiolucent lines as a predictor of progression in congenital pseudarthrosis of the tibia.
articles.authors: Zhang S, Wang T, Zeng L, Xiao B, Mei H, Mao X, et al.
articles.population: Children with congenital pseudarthrosis of the tibia (Crawford types I to III)
articles.outcomes: Presence of radiolucent lines on X-rays as a predictor of fracture; fracture-free survival over time
articles.take_home: Radiolucent lines visible on X-rays are strongly associated with an increased risk of fracture in children with congenital pseudarthrosis of the tibia. Using radiolucent lines alongside the Crawford classification may help doctors better predict which patients are at higher risk and need closer monitoring or earlier treatment.

articles.title: Indications for revision following Birmingham Hip Resurfacing : insights from the largest 25-year series from a design centre.
articles.authors: Nasser AAHH, Samra I, Treacy RBC, Hussain S
articles.study_type: Retrospective cohort analysis of revision indications
articles.population: Patients who underwent Birmingham Hip Resurfacing between July 1997 and July 2022
articles.sample_size: 4,513 BHR cases over 25 years, with 392 revisions (8.7%)
articles.outcomes: Revision rates by sex, age, and implant head size; indications for revision including aseptic loosening, adverse reaction to metal debris, and periprosthetic fractures
articles.take_home: Men had much lower revision rates (4.7%) compared to women (17.8%), and larger implant heads (50mm or more) had better outcomes than smaller ones. The most common reasons for revision were loosening of the implant and reactions to metal debris, with metal reactions occurring many years after surgery in women.

articles.title: Higher femoral periprosthetic fracture rate with dual-mobility compared with single-mobility total hip arthroplasty : a retrospective propensity-matched study of 780 uncemented hips.
articles.authors: Komat M, Sabot L, Simion F, Lechien D, Bhogal H, Gan El E, et al.
articles.population: Patients undergoing uncemented total hip replacement
articles.outcomes: Periprosthetic fracture rate, dislocation rate, and mortality
articles.take_home: Dual-mobility hip implants were much better at preventing hip dislocation but were associated with a higher rate of fractures around the implant compared with standard implants. The choice between them needs to balance these different risks.

articles.title: Evaluation of the wound healing effects of a hydrogel containing hydroalcoholic extract of Chelidonium majus in a rat model.
articles.authors: Farabi MM, Valiallahi J, Rezanejad-Gatabi Z, Livani Z, Mirhoseini M
articles.population: Adult male Wistar rats
articles.outcomes: Wound closure rate, tissue regeneration, gene expression (TGF-beta, TNF-alpha, IL-1beta)
articles.take_home: A hydrogel dressing containing Chelidonium majus plant extract at 5% concentration accelerated wound closure and improved tissue healing in rats compared to control dressings. The treatment appeared to work by reducing inflammation and supporting new cell growth.

articles.title: Comparative preclinical evaluation of an investigational topical hemostatic formulation against an active commercial comparator in rat arterial, venous and liver bleeding models under normal and heparinized conditions.
articles.authors: Kaplan M, Coban A, Sorar M
articles.population: Adult male Wistar albino rats
articles.outcomes: Time to stop bleeding, blood loss from liver injury, rebleeding after manipulation, operative field quality
articles.take_home: A new experimental topical haemostatic agent stopped bleeding faster than a commercial product across different types of bleeding injury in rats, both with and without blood thinners. The new agent also appeared to reduce rebleeding and keep the surgical area cleaner, though some findings were not statistically significant.
